text:
Ben: After upgrading the OS package to redwoodctl 0.15.0 my per-user profiles disappeared. `redwoodctl auth list` shows nothing. Anyone hit this on Debian/Ubuntu?
Shou: We changed the default config location in 0.15.0 from `~/.redwood` to `~/.config/redwood` but the migration should run on first launch.
Ben: Logs show the migration path but it reported "migration: no migration needed" and then: `fs: rename /home/ben/.redwood -> /home/ben/.config/redwood failed: permission denied`.
Priya: How did you install the package? If dpkg/rpm maintainer scripts ran as root during upgrade they can't operate on user home directories safely.
Ben: Yup, plain `apt upgrade` as root on the box. Looks like the postinst tried to move files as root and hit permission/ownership issues because dotfiles belonged to the user.
Shou: Workaround: run the migration as the user and fix ownership after. Example: 
```
# as the affected user
mkdir -p ~/.config
redwoodctl migrate-config --from ~/.redwood --to ~/.config/redwood
# ensure ownership is correct if you used sudo earlier
sudo chown -R $(id -u):$(id -g) ~/.config/redwood
```
Ben: That recovered my profiles. Suggestion: the package should not attempt per-user file ops during system upgrades. Instead set a marker and let the first non-root CLI invocation perform the migration with a clear prompt.
Priya: Agreed. I'll open a packaging MR to change maintainer scripts and add a small login-time helper that runs `redwoodctl migrate-config` for existing dotfiles.
packaging-bot: Issue created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwoodctl/issues/6010  "packaging: defer per-user config migration to first-run non-root process; avoid root-owned moves" (labels: packaging, devex)
Shou: Nice. Also add a `redwoodctl doctor --migration-check` command to detect stale `~/.redwood` directories and offer an automated fix in CI images.
Ben: Thanks all, glad this is actionable — saved our CI and a few developer laptops.
